content: 1. Ethinylestradiol and Nemolizumab: Nemolizumab can decrease the levels of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 enzyme activity. This may require close monitoring and potential dosage adjustments of ethinylestradiol. 2. Ethinylestradiol and Neomycin (oral): Neomycin reduces the effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 3. Ethinylestradiol and Nicardipine/Nilotinib: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Ethinylestradiol and Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: These drugs increase the metabolism of ethinylestradiol, reducing its effectiveness. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are advised for the remainder of the cycle. 5. Ethinylestradiol and Nitrofurantoin/Ofloxacin: These antibiotics may reduce the effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is advised. 6. Ethinylestradiol and Olanzapine: Ethinylestradiol increases olanzapine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 7. Ferrous Fumarate and Omadacycline: Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of omadacycline in the gastrointestinal tract. Dosing should be separated to avoid interaction. 8. Ferrous Fumarate and Omeprazole/Pantoprazole/Rabeprazole: These drugs reduce the absorption of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. Monitoring is advised. 9. Ethinylestradiol and Oteseconazole: Oteseconazole increases the effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters, potentially increasing toxicity. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 10. Ferrous Fumarate and Pancrelipase: Pancrelipase decreases the levels of ferrous fumarate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. Monitoring is recommended. 11. Ethinylestradiol and Penicillin G/VK: These antibiotics may reduce the effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora or increasing metabolism. Monitoring is advised due to the risk of contraceptive failure. 12. Ethinylestradiol and Pioglitazone: Pioglitazone decreases ethinylestradiol levels through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 13. Ethinylestradiol and Posaconazole/Quinupristin-Dalfopristin: These drugs increase ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 14. Ethinylestradiol and Ramelteon/Rasagiline: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 15. Ethinylestradiol and Rucaparib: Rucaparib increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustments may be required. 16. Ferrous Fumarate and Tetracyclines (e.g., Sarecycline): Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of tetracyclines. Dosing should be separated to avoid interaction. 17. Ethinylestradiol and Selegiline: Ethinylestradiol increases selegiline levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 18. Ethinylestradiol and Tacrolimus: Ethinylestradiol increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 19. Ethinylestradiol and Tizanidine: Ethinylestradiol increases tizanidine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring for adverse effects such as hypotension or bradycardia is recommended. 20. Ferrous Fumarate and Calcium Salts (e.g., Calcium Carbonate): Calcium salts reduce the absorption of ferrous fumarate. Dosing should be separated to avoid interaction. 21. Ethinylestradiol and Tricyclic Antidepressants (e.g., Amitriptyline, Nortriptyline): Ethinylestradiol may increase the plasma concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants by inhibiting their metabolism, potentially increasing adverse effects. 22. Ethinylestradiol and Amobarbital: Amobarbital reduces the effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 23. Ethinylestradiol and Antidiabetics (e.g., Albiglutide): Ethinylestradiol may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitoring glycemic control is advised. 24. Ethinylestradiol and Benzodiazepines (e.g., Alprazolam): Ethinylestradiol may increase benzodiazepine levels by inhibiting their metabolism, potentially increasing sedation or other adverse effects. 25. Ethinylestradiol and Aminocaproic Acid: Concomitant use may lead to additive hypercoagulability due to increased clotting factor production and inhibition of fibrinolysis. Monitoring is recommended. 26. Ethinylestradiol and Rosuvastatin: Rosuvastatin increases ethinylestradiol levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitoring is advised. 27. Ethinylestradiol and Ruxolitinib: Ethinylestradiol increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 28. Ethinylestradiol and Trazodone: Ethinylestradiol may increase trazodone levels by inhibiting its metabolism, potentially increasing adverse effects. 29. Ethinylestradiol and Vitamin E: Vitamin E reduces the absorption of ferrous fumarate. Monitoring is recommended. 30. Ethinylestradiol and Alosetron: Ethinylestradiol increases alosetron levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 31. Ethinylestradiol and Clarithromycin: Ethinylestradiol increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 32. Ethinylestradiol and Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 33. Ethinylestradiol and Danazol: Danazol increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 34. Ethinylestradiol and Duloxetine: Ethinylestradiol increases duloxetine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 35. Ethinylestradiol and Frovatriptan: Ethinylestradiol increases frovatriptan levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 36. Ethinylestradiol and Gymnema: Gymnema reduces the absorption of ferrous fumarate. Monitoring is advised. 37. Ethinylestradiol and Lenvatinib: Lenvatinib increases ethinylestradiol levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 38. Ethinylestradiol and Mineral Oil: Mineral oil reduces the absorption of ethinylestradiol. Monitoring is advised. 39. Ethinylestradiol and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases ethinylestradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 40. Ethinylestradiol and Ruxolitinib Topical: Ethinylestradiol increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 41. Ethinylestradiol and Tizanidine: Ethinylestradiol increases tizanidine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 42. Ethinylestradiol and Tricyclic Antidepressants (e.g., Trimipramine): Ethinylestradiol may increase tricyclic antidepressant levels by inhibiting their metabolism, potentially increasing adverse effects. 43. Ethinylestradiol and Albiglutide: Ethinylestradiol may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of albiglutide. Monitoring glycemic control is recommended. 44. Ethinylestradiol and Amobarbital: Amobarbital reduces the effectiveness of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. This summary highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when these interactions occur.
